rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Righteousness has ranks: Abraham still asks to join those who preceded him, and God answers that he belongs among the righteous in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: فإذا تأملت ذلك حق التأمل قضيت بأن الصلاح ذو مراتب بعضها فوق بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He suggests Abraham may have asked to join Muhammad and the Prophet’s purified family, whose higher righteousness he says Muhammad claims for himself.
rows.anchor: أن إبراهيم عليه السلام سأل اللحوق بمحمد صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وآله الطاهرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of Abraham’s bequest to his sons is the religious way, the milla.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى { ووصى بها إبراهيم بنيه } ، أي وصى بالملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because death is involuntary, the prohibition means to remain firmly Muslim so death does not find one outside Islam.
rows.anchor: النهي عن الموت وهو أمر غير اختياري للإنسان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited declaration that religion with God is Islam confirms that Islam is the religion Abraham brought and that his descendants inherited.
rows.anchor: إن الدين عند الله الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac fathers uses father for an ancestor, uncle, or parent without ellipsis; this supports Abraham’s later address to Azar as father.
rows.anchor: إطلاق لفظ الأب على الجد والعم والوالد من غير مصحح للتغليب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concise phrase “one God” after naming Jacob’s and his fathers’ God prevents the mistaken inference that they worship different gods, as polytheists do.
rows.anchor: في هذا الإيجاز بعد الإطناب بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their submission explains that worship must follow Islam; Islam alone is Abraham’s religion inherited by Isaac, Jacob, Ishmael, Israelites, and Abraham’s descendants, leaving no warrant to replace it.
rows.anchor: بيان للعبادة وأنها ليست عبادة كيفما اتفقت بل عبادة على نهج الإسلام

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Samaʿa reports al-Sadiq’s analogy: faith relates to Islam as the Kaaba to the sacred precinct; one can be in the precinct without being in the Kaaba, but not vice versa.
rows.anchor: عن سماعة عن الصادق عليه السلام الإيمان من الإسلام بمنزلة الكعبة الحرام من الحرم

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Samaʿa reports al-Sadiq defining Islam as professing God’s oneness and affirming the Messenger, which protects life and governs marriage, inheritance, and public status; faith is inward guidance and confirmation.
rows.anchor: عن سماعة أيضا عن الصادق عليه السلام قال الإسلام شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله والتصديق برسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding reports describe the first level of Islam and faith.
rows.anchor: وهي تدل على ما مر بيانه من المرتبة الأولى من الإسلام والإيمان

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Burqi transmits from Ali that Islam means surrender and surrender is certainty; the author places this and the next report at the third level of faith and Islam.
rows.anchor: عن علي عليه السلام قال الإسلام هو التسليم، والتسليم هو اليقين

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says even people who worship, pray, give alms, fast, and pilgrimage become polytheists if they inwardly object to God’s or His Messenger’s acts; the author classifies this as the third level.
rows.anchor: ثم قالوا لشيء صنعه الله أو صنعه رسول الله

rows.speaker: الله
rows.claim: In a Miʿraj report to Ahmad, God calls the happiest life constant remembrance, gratitude, awareness of divine rights, and seeking God’s pleasure day and night.
rows.anchor: قال الله سبحانه يا أحمد هل تدري أي عيش أهنىء وأي حيوة أبقى

rows.speaker: الله
rows.claim: The same report describes lasting life as preferring God’s will, diminishing worldly attractions, guarding the heart from Satan, and becoming inwardly illuminated by divine love.
rows.anchor: وأما الحياة الباقية فهي التى يعمل لنفسه حتى تهون عليه الدنيا،

rows.speaker: الله
rows.claim: Those who act for God’s pleasure receive gratitude, remembrance, and love free of their opposites; God then discloses hidden knowledge and eases death, the grave, and judgment.
rows.anchor: فمن عمل برضاي ألزمه ثلاث خصال أعرفه شكرا لا يخالطه الجهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Miʿraj report concerns the fourth level of Islam and faith.
rows.anchor: وهذا مقام الراضين فمن عمل برضاي ألزمه ثلاث خصال

rows.speaker: حارثة بن مالك
rows.claim: Asked by the Prophet about true faith, Haritha says he has renounced worldly life, stays awake and thirsty, and seems to witness the Throne, Paradise, and Hell; the Prophet says God illuminated his heart and urges him to remain firm.
rows.anchor: يا حارثة بن مالك النعماني؟ فقال يا رسول الله مؤمن حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Haritha report concerns the fourth level of Islam and faith; reports about each level’s details will follow elsewhere, and Qur’anic verses support them.
rows.anchor: والروايتان تحومان حوم المرتبة الرابعة من الإسلام والإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each level of Islam and faith has a corresponding form of unbelief or association; the subtler and higher the level, the harder it is to escape its counterpart.
rows.anchor: لكل مرتبة من مراتب الإسلام والإيمان معنى من الكفر والشرك يقابله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lower level of Islam or faith does not prevent the presence and effects of higher-level unbelief or association; this explains Qur’anic inner readings beyond a verse’s outward application.
rows.anchor: كل مرتبة من مراتب الإسلام والإيمان الدانية، لا ينافي الكفر

rows.speaker: الإمام عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report on “We have more” interprets the added reward as beholding God’s mercy.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام النظر إلى رحمة الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet reports God’s promise to the righteous of what no eye has seen, no ear heard, and no human heart imagined; the author says these reports follow from his account of righteousness.
rows.anchor: أعددت لعبادي الصالحين ما لا عين رأت، ولا أذن سمعت

rows.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Baqir says Jacob’s question about his sons’ worship at death applies to the Qaʾim.
rows.anchor: عن الباقر عليه السلام أنها جرت في القائم

rows.speaker: الصافي
rows.claim: Al-Safi proposes that the application is to the Qaʾim from Muhammad’s family: each of them asks his sons this question at death and receives the same answer.
rows.anchor: قال في الصافي لعل مراده أنها في قائم آل محمد فكل قائم منهم يقول ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse depicts deeds taking embodied form: choosing a small price becomes eating fire, then is recast as choosing misguidance over guidance and punishment over forgiveness; their visible persistence is concealment.
rows.anchor: ذكر أولا أن اختيارهم الثمن القليل على ما أنزل الله هو أكل النار في بطونهم

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq interprets “how patient they are with the Fire” as their persistence in doing what they know will lead to it.
rows.anchor: قال ما أصبرهم على فعل ما يعلمون أنه يصيرهم إلى النار

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Another report from al-Sadiq reads the phrase as “how bold they are toward the Fire.”
rows.anchor: قال ما أجرأهم على النار

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: A third report from al-Sadiq reads it as their diligence in deeds characteristic of the people of the Fire; the author says all three readings are close, the latter two returning to the first sense.
rows.anchor: وعن الصادق عليه السلام ما أعملهم بأعمال أهل النار

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq identifies the transgressor as a game hunter and the aggressor as a thief; neither may eat carrion under necessity or shorten prayer.
rows.anchor: قال الباغي باغي الصيد، والعادي السارق

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Other al-Sadiq reports identify the transgressor as an oppressor and the aggressor as a usurper, or as one rebelling against the Imam and a thief.
rows.anchor: قال الباغي الظالم، والعادي الغاصب

rows.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام وأبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Baqir and al-Sadiq explain the terms as refusing to rebel against the Muslim Imam and not transgressing through disobedience to the path of truth.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام وأبي عبد الله عليه السلام غير باغ على إمام المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The varied glosses of transgressor and aggressor enumerate concrete cases and support the apparent meaning of the words.
rows.anchor: والجميع من قبيل عد المصاديق، وهي تؤيد المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbeliever lacks a divine guardian and is left to desires, imagination, and harmful sensations; God guards believers, while Satan and false patrons lead unbelievers from light into darkness and fear.
rows.anchor: وأما غير المؤمن فلا ولي له يتولى أمره، بل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers receive a new spiritual life and divine light that lets them see their path and discern good from evil, unlike unbelievers who stumble in darkness.
rows.anchor: فدل على أن خبط الكافر في مشيه لكونه واقعا في الظلمات لا يبصر شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who believe in God and the Last Day do not ally with God’s opponents even when they are close relatives; faith is inscribed in their hearts and strengthened by a spirit from God.
rows.anchor: لا تجد قوما يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر يوادون من حاد الله ورسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “a company” means a group; the ones claiming they could not face Goliath are those who drank from the river, while those who abstained answer them.
rows.anchor: الفئة القطعة من الناس، والتدبر في الآيات يعطي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Expecting to meet God” may mean certainty of meeting Him or serve as a figure for humility.
rows.anchor: والظن بلقاء الله إما بمعنى اليقين به وإما كناية عن الخشوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abstainers argue from an observed case of a small force winning by God’s permission, rather than merely saying it is possible, to make their argument more persuasive.
rows.anchor: أخذا بالواقع في الاحتجاج بإراءة المصداق ليكون أقنع للخصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They appeared before Goliath” uses appearance for emerging to battle; pouring patience is a subtle implied metaphor for God imparting it according to each person’s capacity.
rows.anchor: البروز هو الظهور، ومنه البراز وهو الظهور للحرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Firming the feet is a metonym for steadfastness and not fleeing; “they routed them” means they drove them back.
rows.anchor: وكذا تثبيت الاقدام كناية عن الثبات وعدم الفرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The corruption prevented by God’s repelling people means breakdown of human society; damage to the physical earth is only a secondary consequence.
rows.anchor: المراد بفساد الأرض فساد من على الأرض أي فساد الاجتماع الإنساني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human flourishing requires cooperation and social unity, formed through reciprocal influence and resistance; without social checks on acts that harm others’ interests, society disintegrates. The primary social instinct is use, while cooperation and civilization are secondary.
rows.anchor: أن الأصل الأول الفطري للإنسان المكون للاجتماع هو الاستخدام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report promises Abu al-Dahdah a tended date palm in Paradise; the author says it is transmitted through many routes.
rows.anchor: كم من عذق مدلل لأبي الدحداح في الجنة

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq reports that when the Prophet asked for more reward after learning one good deed brings a better reward, God revealed tenfold reward; after another request, God revealed the multiplied loan, showing divine generosity is without limit.
rows.anchor: وفي المعاني عن الصادق عليه السلام لما نزلت هذه الآية من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase that God contracts and expands points to the limitless measure of His giving; the report also appears in al-Tabarsi, al-Ayyashi, and Sunni sources.
rows.anchor: إذ لا حد يحد عطائه تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu al-Hasan interprets the charitable loan as support for the Imam; the author says this is an example of applying a general verse to one instance.
rows.anchor: في الآية، قال هي صلة الإمام

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ identifies the prophet of the Israelites as Samuel, rendered Ismail in Arabic; the author notes Sunni reports and the Biblical form Samuel.
rows.anchor: هو أشموئيل، وهو بالعربية إسماعيل

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Qummi transmits from al-Baqir that after Moses the Israelites sinned and changed God’s religion; their disobeyed prophet may have been Jeremiah, and the Copt Goliath then conquered, killed, displaced, and enslaved them.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام أن بني إسرائيل بعد موت موسى عملوا بالمعاصي،

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Israelites asked their prophet to request a king for battle; prophetic and royal authority had been held by separate houses, so they sought a ruler rather than a prophet.
rows.anchor: في بيت، والملك والسلطان في بيت آخر

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Israelites objected to Saul’s appointment because he lacked wealth and they believed themselves more entitled; their prophet answered that God chose him for superior knowledge and stature, though he was poor.
rows.anchor: فقال لهم نبيهم إن الله اصطفاه عليكم وزاده بسطة في العلم والجسم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: The return of the Ark was Saul’s sign; it contained God-given tranquility and relics of Moses and Aaron, and angels carried it. The remnant is interpreted as prophetic descendants.
rows.anchor: إن آية ملكه أن يأتيكم التابوت فيه سكينة من ربكم وبقية مما ترك آل موسى وآل هارون

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Ark had held the tablets, Moses’ armor, and prophetic signs; Joshua kept it, but Israelites later neglected it until God removed it. They remained honored while it was among them, and it returned when Saul was appointed.
rows.anchor: فلما حضر موسى الوفاة وضع فيه الألواح ودرعه وما كان عنده من آيات النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that the prophet was Jeremiah is an interpolation within the larger narration; “they turned back except a few” means most refused the command to fight.
rows.anchor: أرميا النبي، رواية معترضة في رواية

rows.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report from al-Rida, also transmitted by al-Ayyashi from al-Baqir, says the few who remained obedient numbered sixty thousand.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار أن هذا القليل كانوا ستين ألفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report places prophecy in Levi’s house and kingship in Joseph’s; the alternative puts kingship in Judah’s house, but this is challenged because Judah had no earlier king, whereas Joseph himself was a king. Imami reports support Joseph’s house.
rows.anchor: وهذا يؤيد ما ورد في أحاديث أئمة أهل البيت ان الملك كان في بيت يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “remnant” is the narrator’s gloss, not al-Baqir’s wording; al-Sadiq independently explains the relics as descendants of prophets.
rows.anchor: والبقية ذرية الأنبياء، وهم من الراوي

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Baqir reports that after the river test only 313 men remained, some having scooped water and others abstained; at Goliath’s approach the groups voiced opposite judgments of their chances.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في حديث وقال الله إن الله مبتليكم بنهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports from both Imami and Sunni sources often count the survivors with Saul as 313, matching the number at Badr; the verse’s exception supports assigning the “no power” statement to those who scooped and the reassurance to those who did not drink.
rows.anchor: وأما كون الباقين مع طالوت ثلثمائة وثلاثة عشر رجلا بعدد أهل بدر فقد كثر فيه الروايات

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says the angels carried the Ark in the form of a cow.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله تعالى إن آية ملكه إلى قوله تحمله الملائكة قال كانت تحمله في صورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains that he usually omits chains when a report conforms to the Qur’an, but gives a chain when no such alignment is available; he still selects sound reports or those supported by indications.
rows.anchor: لأن إسقاط الأسانيد فيه إنما هو لمكان موافقه القرآن ومعه لا حاجة إلى ذكر سند الحديث

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Ayyashi transmits al-Sadiq’s account of David, youngest of four brothers, left tending his elderly father’s sheep while Saul marched; his father sent him with provisions, and David was small but pure-hearted.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن محمد الحلبي عن الصادق عليه السلام،

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: On the way, a stone called David to take it and kill Goliath; David placed it with his sling stones. Though the soldiers feared Goliath, David said he would kill him and demonstrated courage to Saul.
rows.anchor: فمر داود على حجر فقال الحجر يا داود خذني واقتل بي جالوت

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: David told Saul he had rescued sheep from a lion by prying open its jaws; Saul fitted him with armor and hoped God would let him defeat Goliath.
rows.anchor: قال كان الأسد يعدو على الشاة من غنمي فأدركه فآخذ برأسه فأفك لحييه

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: At battle David struck Goliath between the eyes with a stone, killing him; Israel then rallied to David, who received the Psalms, mastery of iron, and the ability to lead mountains and birds in praise.
rows.anchor: فلما رآه أخذ الحجر فجعله في مقذافه فرماه فصك به بين عينيه فدمغه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A shepherd’s sling is called a miqdāf; reports from both sides agree that David killed Goliath with a stone.
rows.anchor: به الأحجار، وقد اتفقت ألسنة الأخبار من طرق الفريقين

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ reports from Ali that the tranquility in the Ark was a gentle wind from Paradise with a human-like face; similar reports come through Sunni sources and al-Rida.
rows.anchor: قال إن السكينة التي كانت فيه ريح هفانة من الجنة لها وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though solitary, these reports can be read plausibly as tranquility being a level of the soul that brings calm obedience to God, figuratively expressed as the spirit of faith.
rows.anchor: فإن المراد بها على تقدير صحتها أن السكينة مرتبة من مراتب النفس في الكمال

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu al-Hasan calls the tranquility a speaking spirit of God that informed Israelites when they disagreed; the author interprets it as the spirit of faith guiding believers to the right answer.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام روح الله يتكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Natural science describes organisms as competing for survival: stronger, more complete individuals prevail while weaker ones disappear, yielding struggle for existence and natural selection or survival of the fittest.
rows.anchor: إحداهما تنازع البقاء، والثانية الانتخاب الطبيعي وبقاء الأمثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Social theorists apply struggle and selection to societies: cohesive communities respecting individual and collective rights are likelier to endure; history links collapse to division, hypocrisy, injustice, corrupt elites, and lost seriousness.
rows.anchor: فالاجتماع الكامل وهو الاجتماع المبني على أساس الاتحاد الكامل المحكم المرعي فيه حقوق الأفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author illustrates natural selection with extinct ancient animals and species such as crocodiles and frogs that survive in diminished forms; current species also change under competition, with the fittest persisting through heredity.
rows.anchor: ولم يعمل في إفنائها وانقراضها إلا تنازع البقاء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Later thinkers challenge universal selection because weak species persist, and cultivated plants and animals improve while their wild counterparts remain inferior or weaken, with heredity preserving both patterns.
rows.anchor: وقد ناقضه المتأخرون بكثير من الأنواع الضعيفة الوجود الباقية بين الأنواع حتى اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some explain survival through dependence on the environment: combined temporal, spatial, and natural conditions fit a creature to its habitat; fit organisms survive and unfit ones perish, so struggle and selection derive from this law.
rows.anchor: فالمحيط الموجود وهو مجموع العوامل الطبيعية تحت شرائط خاصة زمانية ومكانية يستدعي تبعية الموجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Environmental dependence also has counterexamples and does not operate universally.
rows.anchor: ولكن لقاعدة تبعية المحيط من النقض في اطرادها نظير ما للقاعدتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If environmental adaptation or natural selection were universal, no ill-fitted forms, weak species beside strong ones, or declining and improving breeds would remain; scientific research therefore treats these laws as valid only in some cases.
rows.anchor: فالحق كما ربما اعترفت به الأبحاث العلمية أن هذه القواعد على ما فيها من الصحة في الجملة غير مطردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general philosophical account is causality: material things act to preserve themselves and affect others; stronger causes alter weaker things, which explains competition, selection, and environmental adaptation.
rows.anchor: فكل موجود من الموجودات المادية بمالها من الصورة الفعالة لنفع وجوده يوجه أثره إلى غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such laws affect a thing’s accidents and attributes, not its essence or conversion into another kind; naturalists accept species change because they deny substantial essences and reduce species to arrangements of common matter and accidents.
rows.anchor: في عوارض وجود الشيء ولواحقه

rows.speaker: مفسر لم يسمه المؤلف
rows.claim: An unnamed exegete reads God’s repelling people as struggle for existence and natural selection, using the permission to fight, defense of worship places, and eventual victory of believers as evidence.
rows.anchor: ذكر بعض المفسرين ان قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: مفسر لم يسمه المؤلف
rows.claim: The same exegete reads the water and foam parable as destructive falsehood being expelled while useful truth remains and grows in society.
rows.anchor: فهو يفيد ان سيول الحوادث وميزان التنازع تقذف زبد الباطل الضار في الاجتماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author accepts competition and selection as broadly real but rejects these verses as evidence that they are what the verses intend to teach.
rows.anchor: لكن هذين الصنفين الذين أوردهما من الآيات غير مسوقين لبيان شيء من القاعدتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permission-to-fight passage teaches that God’s will and truth cannot be defeated: believers prevail as bearers of truth and victims of injustice, because God supports truthful bearers of the right, not because physical strength selects the fittest.
rows.anchor: لا يقدر على أن يدحض حجة الحق إذا تقابلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conclusion that all affairs belong to God points to the cosmos moving toward truth, sincerity, and genuine happiness; the Qur’an elsewhere promises victory to God and His messengers.
rows.anchor: يشير به إلى عدة آيات تفيد أن الكون يسير في طريق كماله إلى الحق والصدق والسعادة الحقيقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites promises that God and His messengers will prevail and that God governs His affair, showing divine victory over all things.
rows.anchor: والله غالب على أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water-and-foam parable concerns truth enduring and falsehood vanishing, whether competing material things, spiritual meaning over matter, or spiritual realities opposed to one another; meaning prevails without struggle.
rows.anchor: مسوقة لبيان بقاء الحق وزهوق الباطل سواء كان على نحو التنازع كما في الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Transmitted history preserves broad and small events and serves social memory, reflection, storytelling, entertainment, and political, economic, and practical needs.
rows.anchor: والإنسان ينتفع به في جهات شتى من حياته كالاجتماع والاعتبار والقص والحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rulers distort history to promote useful facts, hide damaging ones, or dress falsehood as truth, following the self-interest shared by individuals and societies.
rows.anchor: الحكومات المقتدرة في كل عصر تهتم بإفشاء ما تنتفع به من الحقائق وستر ما تستضر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Transmitters and historians introduce sectarian, religious, national, and ideological bias; records usually support their own doctrine, whether in past religious histories or modern materialist accounts.
rows.anchor: المتحملين للأخبار والناقلين لها والمؤلفين فيها جميعهم لا يخلون من إعمال الإحساسات الباطنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier history lacked dependable ways to preserve and transmit records; modern communications ease that problem, but politics now penetrates all life and changes what is disclosed, hidden, or revised.
rows.anchor: وهذا مما يوجب سوء الظن بالتاريخ حتى كاد أن يورده مورد السقوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These distortions explain scholars’ turn to archaeology, but material evidence also remains vulnerable to historians’ biases and political alteration.
rows.anchor: وهذا وإن سلمت عن بعض الاشكالات المذكورة كالأول مثلا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is divine revelation free of error and need not yield to unreliable transmitted history; its account of Saul often differs from the manipulated Biblical histories, whose author is unknown.
rows.anchor: فلا نبالي بمخالفة القرآن لما يوجد منافيا له في التواريخ وخاصة في كتب العهدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is a guide rather than a history book: it selects details needed for reflection, warning, wisdom, and moral instruction, omitting connective events in the Saul and Goliath story as it does throughout its narratives.
rows.anchor: وإنما هو كلام إلهي مفرغ في قالب الوحي يهدي به الله من اتبع رضوانه سبل السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an calls people to observe the outcomes of earlier communities: their histories reveal established patterns and serve as public explanation, guidance, and warning to the mindful.
rows.anchor: قد خلت من قبلكم سنن فسيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He defines the key terms: mutual debt, dictation, shortchanging, weariness, causing harm, disobedience, and the two plural forms for pledged collateral.
rows.anchor: والاملال والاملاء إلقاء الرجل للكاتب ما يكتبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using “the one who owes the right” instead of a pronoun removes possible confusion with the previously mentioned writer.
rows.anchor: لرفع اللبس برجوع الضمير إلى الكاتب السابق ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit pronoun in “he cannot dictate” makes the debtor share the work with his guardian; unlike earlier cases, the guardian handles only what the debtor cannot.
rows.anchor: فإن هذه الصورة تغاير الصورتين الأوليين بأن الولي في الصورتين الأوليين هو المسؤول بالأمر المستقل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Lest one of them err” elliptically means fearing that one woman will err; repeating “one of them” distinguishes the initially unspecified woman from the one who reminds after the other errs.
rows.anchor: والنكتة فيه اختلاف معنى اللفظ في الموضعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear God concerns obeying the instructions in the verse; “God teaches you” begins a separate statement of favor, teaching religious rules and lawful and unlawful matters.
rows.anchor: فالمراد به الامتنان بتعليم شرائع الدين ومسائل الحلال والحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although piety can bring divine teaching elsewhere, the verse does not establish that causal rule: the conjunction and the passage’s structure do not support it.
rows.anchor: فيه أنه وإن كان حقا يدل عليه الكتاب والسنة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating God’s name shows that “God teaches you” is independent; the final name emphasizes the reason for His instruction, that He knows everything.
rows.anchor: أظهر الاسم أولا وثانيا لوقوعه في كلامين مستقلين، وأظهر ثالثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two verses contain nearly twenty legal rulings, including rules for debt and pledges; detailed legal debate belongs in jurisprudence, so he leaves it aside here.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الآيتين تدلان على ما يقرب من عشرين حكما من أصول أحكام الدين والرهن وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This closing verse summarizes the surah’s detailed instruction and draws its result.
rows.anchor: بيان الآية بمنزلة الفذلكة لتفصيل البيان الوارد في السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unrestricted command to be patient covers hardship, obedience to God, and avoiding disobedience; its singular form contrasts with collective mutual endurance.
rows.anchor: فالصبر يراد به الصبر على الشدائد والصبر في طاعة الله والصبر عن معصيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual patience is shared endurance in which people rely on one another, strengthening the quality and multiplying its effect through cooperation.
rows.anchor: والمصابرة هي التصبر وتحمل الأذى جماعة باعتماد صبر البعض على صبر آخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribāṭ is broader: it binds a community’s strengths and actions across all religious affairs in hardship and ease; the commands aim at complete happiness in both worlds, so they conclude with piety and true success.
rows.anchor: أعم معنى من المصابرة وهي إيجاد الجماعة الارتباط بين قواهم وأفعالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings are inherently social, as history, social organization, and several Qur’anic passages affirm; people are made into peoples and tribes to know one another and depend on one another.
rows.anchor: كون النوع الإنساني نوعا اجتماعيا لا يحتاج في إثباته إلى كثير بحث فكل فرد من هذا النوع مفطور على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human social organization, like other spiritual traits, developed gradually alongside material and moral capacities rather than appearing complete at humanity’s beginning.
rows.anchor: الاجتماع الإنساني كسائر الخواص الروحية الإنسانية وما يرتبط بها لم يوجد حين وجد تاما كاملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earliest form was the household founded through marriage, because reproduction most directly requires more than one person; this grew into “use,” subordinating others to meet one’s needs by imposing authority and will.
rows.anchor: أول ما ظهر من الاجتماع فيه الاجتماع المنزلي بالازدواج لكون عامله الطبيعي وهو جهاز التناسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Use developed into household, clan, tribal, and national leadership; the initial leader was chosen by strength and courage, then wealth and descendants, and ultimately skill in government and politics.
rows.anchor: ثم برز ذلك في صورة الرئاسة كرئيس المنزل ورئيس العشيرة ورئيس القبيلة ورئيس الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This hierarchy was the initial cause of idolatry, according to the author, and has continued to the present.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو السبب الابتدائي لظهور الوثنية وقيامها على ساقها حتى اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Society persisted through these stages without people consciously isolating it as a value; it grew under other concerns such as use and defense, until prophecy first drew explicit attention to preserving it.
rows.anchor: أول ما نبه الإنسان بالاجتماع تفصيلا واعتنى بحفظه استقلالا نبهته به النبوة
